title: Fan charts and pullback of arbitrary saturated fan blowup towers
statement:
For an fs log scheme $(X,M)$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], a strict morphism is a log morphism whose source log structure is the log structure pulled back from its target. On a Zariski log scheme, meaning a log structure associated to one on the Zariski site, a fan chart $c:(X,\overline M)\to(F,\mathcal P_F)$ is a morphism of sharp monoidal spaces inducing an isomorphism $c^{-1}\mathcal P_F\simeq\overline M$, where $F$ is a fine fan [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup].

(i) Every fs log scheme admits strict etale neighborhoods carrying such a fan chart. If $X$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and all characteristic group completions are torsion free, a finite family of quasi-compact strict etale neighborhoods covers $X$, each with a chart to a saturated torsion-free affine fan; quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover.

(ii) Given any fan chart $c$ of an fs log scheme $(V,N)$ and any finite saturated blowup tower $F_\bullet\to F$, there exists a tower $c^*F_\bullet$ of saturated log blowups of $(V,N)$. At a stage with center $J\subset\mathcal P_{F_i}$ its log center is the inverse image in $N_i$ of the ideal generated by $c_i^{-1}J$ in $\overline N_i$. There are fan charts $c_i:(V_i,\overline N_i)\to(F_i,\mathcal P_{F_i})$ at every level. In particular $\overline N_{i,\bar v}\simeq\mathcal P_{F_i,c_i(\bar v)}$. Nonempty coherent centers pull back to nonempty coherent log ideals. These constructions are compatible with composition of fan blowup towers and with strict base change of log schemes; the latter is taken in the fs category.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.3.2--3.3.13, pp.106--109, especially 3.3.4(ii), 3.3.8--3.3.11, 3.3.13(i),(iii); finite cover as in proof of 3.3.15.

proof.text: Choose strict etale fs monoid chart neighborhoods by the fs definition. The fixed-chart sharpening lemma gives their fan charts with saturated torsion-free affine targets. Refine by affine opens; the affine qcqs and etale openness lemmas make their sources quasi-compact and their images an open cover. When $X$ is quasi-compact choose finitely many images; for empty $X$ use the empty family. This proves (i).

For one stage of (ii), the local-monoid-lift lemma supplies, for each $v\in V$ with $z=c(v)$ and $P=\mathcal P_{F,z}$, a Zariski neighborhood on which the given chart $c$ lifts to a sharp fs monoid chart $h:P\to N$. Every open neighborhood of $z$ contains $F_z$, and $z$ is the unique closed point of $F_z\simeq\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$, so $\Gamma(F_z,\mathcal P_F)=P$; as $J$ is coherent, $J|_{F_z}$ is generated by a finite nonempty $E\subset P$. Shrink these neighborhoods to affine opens, on which $h$ is still a chart. Apply the center-and-local-charts lemma to $J$ and $E$: the specified inverse-image center $\mathcal I$ is nonempty coherent, its saturated log blowup $(V\prime,N\prime)$ exists, and on these neighborhoods it has the stated local maps to $F\prime$ and the canonical characteristic-stalk isomorphisms.

The composite $(V\prime,\overline{N\prime})\to(V,\overline N)\to F$ has local stalk maps, since a log morphism maps nonunits of characteristics to nonunits. The ideal generated by the pulled-back $J$ in $\overline{N\prime}$ is Zariski locally principal: on each chart $U\prime_a$ of the center lemma, $h(b)=h(a)+(b-a)$ with $b-a\in R_a$ for $b\in E$, so the image of $a$ generates it. The saturated-fan-lift lemma makes all local maps to $F\prime$ agree on overlaps, independently of the chosen monoid lifts. They therefore glue; the local sheaf isomorphisms in the preceding step make the glued map a fan chart, with the required geometric-stalk identifications.

Induct on the ordered tower length: start at $(V,N),c$, and at stage $i$ perform the preceding one-stage construction on $J_i$. The local-charts lemma ensures each new level is again locally Noetherian fs and Zariski. This gives every center and chart. Concatenation performs the same operations in the same order; uniqueness of log blowup factorization and of the fan lift identifies every level and chart, starting with the identity. The zero-length case is the initial datum.

For strict $g:(W,L)\to(V,N)$, the strict-log-base-change lemma identifies characteristics, shows the composed chart is a fan chart, and identifies its center with $g^{-1}\mathcal I L$. At each stage it gives the unique strict comparison and the fs Cartesian square. Uniqueness of the fan lift identifies their chart maps. Iterate along the ordered centers. The one-stage identity and composition compatibilities yield the tower compatibilities; concatenation and consecutive segments use the identity log morphism, including its section maps.

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII 3.3.2--3.3.13, with the affine monoid constructions in 3.1.1--3.1.25; the local lift and gluing arguments implicit in 3.3.13 are expanded.
